souinStorageEtcd.name: etcd Cache Storage
souinStorageEtcd.description: Keeps the HTTP cache in an etcd cluster, shared by every Caddy that points at it. No authentication.

proxyHosts.customCaddyfileHelp: Caddyfile directives for this host, adapted by Caddy and inserted before the reverse proxy. Rejected on save if Caddy cannot parse them.

proxyHosts.dnsPinningInfoTitle: Hostname upstreams are resolved at config-apply time
proxyHosts.dnsPinningModeHelp: Inherit uses the global setting. Enabled/Disabled overrides per host.
proxyHosts.dnsConnectTimeoutHelp: Caps name lookup and connecting together, e.g. 5s. A connect timeout under Upstream timeouts wins over it
proxyHosts.dnsResolverOverrideDescription: Useful for upstream services that require specific DNS resolution, such as internal DNS or service discovery. Common resolvers: 1.1.1.1 (Cloudflare), 194.242.2.2 (Mullvad), 9.9.9.9 (Quad9).
proxyHosts.dnsResolverOverrideTitle: Per-host resolvers override global DNS settings
proxyHosts.dnsResolversDescription: Configure per-host DNS resolution for upstream discovery and health checks
proxyHosts.dnsResolversHelp: One resolver per line (e.g., 1.1.1.1, 9.9.9.9). Used for dynamic upstream DNS resolution.
proxyHosts.domainsHelp: One per line or comma-separated. Wildcards like *.example.com are supported.
proxyHosts.errorPagesHelp: Serve a custom response body when a request errors (e.g. 502/503 when the upstream is down, or 404). Comma-separate status codes, or leave blank to match every error. The original status code is preserved.
proxyHosts.fallbackResolversHelp: Fallback resolvers if primary fails. One per line.
proxyHosts.forwardAuthAccessDeniedDescription: No users or groups are selected, so forward auth will reject every request.
proxyHosts.forwardAuthApiSplitHelp: A caller that did not ask for HTML - an API client, a WebSocket handshake - gets 401 instead of a redirect to the login page, which it cannot follow.
proxyHosts.forwardAuthBypassHeadersHelp: A request carrying any of these headers skips forward auth entirely, leaving the upstream to check the credential itself. Comma-separated.
proxyHosts.forwardAuthCopyHeadersHelp: Headers taken from the auth server's answer and set on the request sent upstream. One per line. The same headers are stripped from every inbound request, so they cannot be forged.
proxyHosts.forwardAuthDescription: Authenticate through an external forward-auth server, such as Authelia
proxyHosts.forwardAuthExcludedPathsHelp: Paths to exclude from authentication. These paths bypass forward auth while all other paths remain protected. Ignored if Protected Paths is set.
proxyHosts.forwardAuthGroupsEmptyDescription: Create groups on the Groups page.
proxyHosts.forwardAuthProtectedPathsHelp: Leave empty to protect the entire domain. Comma-separated paths to protect specific routes only.
proxyHosts.forwardAuthUpstreamHelp: Where the auth server listens, as seen from Caddy, e.g. http://authelia:9091.
proxyHosts.geoblockAllowPrecedenceHelp: Allow rules take precedence over block rules.
proxyHosts.geoblockDescription: Block or allow traffic by country, continent, ASN, CIDR, or IP
proxyHosts.geoblockFailClosedHelp: Blocks requests where the real client IP cannot be determined, e.g. behind a trusted proxy with no usable X-Forwarded-For. Default: off (fail-open).
proxyHosts.geoblockRedirectHelp: If set, sends a 302 redirect instead of the status/body above
proxyHosts.geoblockResponseBodyHelp: Body text returned to blocked clients
proxyHosts.identityProtectedPathsHelp: Leave empty to require an identity for the whole host. Comma-separated paths gate only those routes.
proxyHosts.internalRewriteHelp: Internally rewrite the request URI before proxying. The client URL is unchanged; the upstream sees the target URI.
proxyHosts.lbChooseHelp: How many upstreams to pick between at random, then send to the least loaded of them.
proxyHosts.lbHealthFailsHelp: Consecutive failed probes before an upstream is taken out.
proxyHosts.lbHealthPassesHelp: Consecutive successful probes before an upstream is used again.
proxyHosts.lbHealthRequestBodyHelp: Sent with the probe. Distinct from the expected response body.
proxyHosts.lbPolicyClientIpHashHelp: Real client IP - set trusted proxies first
proxyHosts.lbPolicyRandomChooseHelp: Least loaded of N at random
proxyHosts.lbPolicyWeightedRoundRobinHelp: Sequential, in proportion to per-upstream weights
proxyHosts.lbQueryKeyHelp: Requests with the same value for this parameter go to the same upstream.
proxyHosts.lbUnhealthyRequestCountHelp: Concurrent requests to one upstream before it is considered unhealthy.
proxyHosts.lbWeightsHelp: Comma-separated, one per upstream and in the same order. A list that does not match the upstreams is ignored.
proxyHosts.loadBalancerDescription: Configure load balancing and health checks for multiple upstreams
proxyHosts.loadBalancerHeaderHelp: The request header to hash for upstream selection
proxyHosts.locationLoadBalancerDescription: Health checks & balancing for this path's upstreams
proxyHosts.locationLoadBalancerLabel: Enable load balancing for this path
proxyHosts.mtlsCertificateBypassHelp: These bypass role checks for this path
proxyHosts.mtlsCertificateSelectionHelp: A certificate must be set. Select roles and/or individual certificates to allow.
proxyHosts.mtlsCertificatesEmptyDescription: Issue certificates from a CA on the Certificates page.
proxyHosts.mtlsDefaultAccessHelp: All trusted certificates and roles have equal access to every path.
proxyHosts.mtlsDenyPathLabel: Deny all access to this path
proxyHosts.mtlsDescription: Require clients to present a trusted certificate to connect
proxyHosts.mtlsExcludedPathsHelp: Paths to exclude from mTLS. These paths bypass client certificate enforcement while all other paths remain protected. Ignored if Protected Paths is set.
proxyHosts.mtlsPathPatternHelp: Use * for all paths, /admin/* for prefix match
proxyHosts.mtlsPathRulesHelp: Restrict specific paths to certain roles or certificates. Paths without rules allow any trusted cert/role above.
proxyHosts.mtlsRolesEmptyDescription: No mTLS roles yet. Create roles on the Certificates page.
proxyHosts.mtlsSubjectsEmptyDescription: No roles or certificates are selected.

proxyHosts.name: Name
proxyHosts.overLimitActionHelpInherit: Uses the action set on the WAF settings page.
proxyHosts.overLimitActionHelpPartial: The request is forwarded whole, but only the part of its body within the limit is inspected - the rest reaches the upstream unchecked.
proxyHosts.overLimitActionHelpReject: A request whose body is over the limit is refused with 413 Payload Too Large and never reaches the upstream.
proxyHosts.owaspCrsHelp: Covers SQLi, XSS, LFI, RCE and hundreds of other attack patterns
proxyHosts.passiveHealthChecksHelp: Mark upstreams unhealthy based on response failures
proxyHosts.pathAllowsHelp: Paths that bypass any matching Path Block and reach the upstream. Allows are folded into every block's matcher: a block fires only for requests that match its pattern and do not match any allow. Example: allow /secret + block /* means only /secret reaches the upstream; everything else returns the block status. Allows do not affect Path Rewrites.
proxyHosts.pathBlocksHelp: Return a static response (no proxying) for matching paths. Supports Caddy path patterns like /dns-query or /admin/*.
proxyHosts.pathPrefixRewriteHelp: Prepend this prefix to every request before proxying (e.g. /recipes → /recipes/original/path)
proxyHosts.cacheAssetsDescription: Cache stylesheets, scripts, images and fonts. Pages and API responses are never cached.
proxyHosts.cacheModeBrowserHelp: Tells browsers to keep assets for the max age, unless the upstream already sets Cache-Control.
proxyHosts.cacheModeCaddyHelp: Caddy also keeps a shared copy, so repeat requests skip the upstream. Responses that set a cookie or are marked private or no-store are never stored.
proxyHosts.cacheMaxAgeHelp: How long an asset stays cached: 60 seconds to one year. 86400 is a day.
proxyHosts.responseHeadersEmptyDescription: No custom headers - use the + button to add one.
proxyHosts.stickyCookieNameHelp: Name of the cookie for sticky sessions
proxyHosts.stickyCookieSecretHelp: Secret key for HMAC cookie signing
proxyHosts.tailnetOnlyHelp: Keep this host off the public :80/:443 listener entirely. Uncheck to publish it in both places.
proxyHosts.tailscaleAuthKeyMissingDescription: Saving will be refused. The node cannot register without a key, and Caddy rejects a configuration whose listener will not come up - that would stop every proxy host from being updated, not just this one. Add a key in Settings → Network → Tailscale first.
proxyHosts.tailscaleAuthKeyMissingTitle: No Tailscale auth key is stored
proxyHosts.tailscaleDescription: Serve this host on your tailnet instead of, or as well as, the public internet
proxyHosts.tailscaleDisabledDescription: This host will not be served at all until Settings → Network → Tailscale is enabled - it is dropped from the configuration rather than published publicly.
proxyHosts.tailscaleDisabledTitle: Tailscale is switched off in Settings
proxyHosts.tailscaleDomainRequirementDescription: Routing is still by Host header, so a request to https://{node}.your-tailnet.ts.net only reaches this host if that name is one of its domains. Caddy gets the certificate for it from Tailscale - no ACME, no DNS provider.
proxyHosts.tailscaleDomainRequirementTitle: Add the node's MagicDNS name to Domains
proxyHosts.tailscaleExcludedPathsHelp: Paths that bypass the identity check while everything else stays gated. Ignored if Protected Paths is set.
proxyHosts.tailscaleForwardIdentityHelp: Sets X-Tailscale-User, -Login, -Name, -Tailnet and -Profile-Picture on the proxied request. Any such header sent by the client is stripped first.
proxyHosts.tailscaleIdentityHelp: Only devices signed in to your tailnet may reach this host, and the caller is identified by their tailnet login. Tagged devices are refused, since they have no user behind them.
proxyHosts.tailscaleNodeHelp: The tailnet machine this host is served on. Empty uses "{node}" from Settings → Network → Tailscale. Several hosts can share one node.
proxyHosts.tailscaleUpstreamNodeHelp: Node to dial the upstreams through, for a backend that only exists on your tailnet. Upstream IP pinning and custom DNS resolvers do not apply - names are resolved by MagicDNS on the far side.
proxyHosts.notesHelp: Anything worth remembering about this host. Only people who can see the host can read them.
proxyHosts.unhealthyLatencyHelp: Latency above which an upstream is marked unhealthy
proxyHosts.upstreamsHelp: Backend servers to proxy requests to
proxyHosts.wafBodyLimitsDescription: Coraza buffers request bodies for inspection and rejects anything larger than its limit - 12.5 MiB with the OWASP CRS loaded. Raise it for hosts that receive large uploads. Leave blank to inherit.
proxyHosts.wafDescription: Inspect and block malicious requests via Coraza / OWASP CRS
proxyHosts.wafRuleExclusionsHelp: Rules listed here are disabled via SecRuleRemoveById
proxyHosts.forceHttpsHelp: Redirect plain HTTP requests to HTTPS
proxyHosts.hstsHelp: Tell browsers to only ever use HTTPS for this host. Requires Force HTTPS
proxyHosts.websocketSupportHelp: Allow WebSocket upgrades. The WAF checks the handshake but not the messages after it
proxyHosts.preserveHostHeaderHelp: Send the original Host header to the upstream instead of the upstream's own address
proxyHosts.hstsSubdomainsHelp: Include subdomains in the Strict-Transport-Security header
proxyHosts.skipHttpsValidationHelp: Skip SSL certificate hostname verification for backend connections
proxyHosts.maintenanceDescription: Answer every request with a 503 while the upstream is being worked on. The domain keeps its certificate, and addresses in the bypass list still reach the upstream
proxyHosts.maintenanceActiveDescription: Only the bypass addresses reach the upstream. Access lists, sign-in and the WAF still apply to them
proxyHosts.maintenanceBypassHelp: IP addresses or CIDR ranges, one per line, that skip the maintenance page - yours, so you can check the site before reopening it. The client IP honours Settings → Network → Trusted Proxies
proxyHosts.maintenanceRetryAfterHelp: Tells clients and crawlers when to come back. Leave it empty to send none
proxyHosts.maintenanceBodyHelp: HTML shown to visitors. Leave it empty to use this host's 503 error page, then the global one, then a built-in page
proxyHosts.anubisDescription: Make browsers solve a proof-of-work challenge from your Anubis instance before they reach the upstream, after geo blocking and the WAF and before any sign-in. Scrapers that cannot run JavaScript never get through
proxyHosts.anubisUpstreamHelp: Where Caddy reaches Anubis, running in subrequest mode (TARGET set to a single space). One instance can serve every host
proxyHosts.anubisExemptPathsHelp: Caddy path patterns, one per line, that skip the challenge. API clients, feeds and webhooks cannot solve one
proxyHosts.rateLimitDescription: Answer clients that send too many requests with 429 Too Many Requests, before geo blocking and the WAF see them.
proxyHosts.rateLimitUnavailable: Rate limiting is not in Caddy
proxyHosts.rateLimitPathsHelp: Caddy path patterns separated by spaces, such as /login or /api/*. Empty covers every request.
proxyHosts.rateLimitWindowInvalid: Use a number and a unit, such as 10s, 1m or 1h
proxyHosts.rateLimitHelp: Each zone allows a number of requests per client in a sliding window. A request over the limit gets a 429 with Retry-After, rendered by this host's error pages. The client IP honours trusted proxies. An IPv6 prefix such as 64 counts a whole network as one client.
proxyHosts.crowdsecDescription: Refuse clients your CrowdSec Local API has a decision against, before rate limiting, geo blocking and the WAF. Applies once CrowdSec is set up under Settings > CrowdSec.
proxyHosts.upstreamTimeoutsDescription: How long to wait on the upstream before giving up. A field left empty keeps Caddy's default, and location rules use the same values
proxyHosts.upstreamTimeoutInvalid: Use a number and a unit, such as 30s, 1m30s or 2h

backup.title: Backup and restore
backup.downloadHelp: Everything this instance is configured with: hosts, certificates and their keys, access lists, users, groups, API tokens and every setting. Secrets are decrypted into the file and the whole file is encrypted with the passphrase, so it restores onto a new machine with a different SESSION_SECRET.
backup.passphraseHelp: At least {min} characters. It is the only thing protecting the file, and nobody can recover a backup without it.
backup.notIncluded: Not included: who is signed in, the certificates Caddy has issued (they are issued again), analytics, and the GeoIP databases (they are downloaded again).
backup.downloadFailed: The backup could not be made
backup.restoreHelp: Replaces this instance's whole configuration with the backup's. What is here now is saved to a backup of its own on the controller's data volume first, with the same passphrase. Everyone is signed out afterwards.
backup.keepAgentsHelp: Leave on when restoring onto the same machine. Turn off when moving to a new one: its agents will pair afresh, and hosts assigned to the old agents serve on every agent.
backup.newerHelp: Upgrade this instance first. An older version would silently drop what it doesn't understand.
backup.confirmHelp: Every host, user and setting here is replaced by the backup's. Caddy's certificates will be issued again, which can hit your certificate authority's rate limits if there are many hosts.

settings.abortResponseDescription: Caddy writes no status line or body - the native equivalent of a “444 / no response” policy.
settings.abortResponseTitle: Unmatched connections are closed without a response
settings.accessLogsCommand: View with: docker exec caddy-proxy-manager-caddy tail -f /logs/access.log
settings.accessLogsInfoTitle: Access logs live in the caddy-logs Docker volume
settings.acmeDirectoryHelp: Leave empty to use the Let's Encrypt default. For an internal CA (OpenBao, Step-CA, Windows ADCS), paste its ACME directory URL - must be HTTPS.
settings.acmeEmailHelp: Used by Let's Encrypt for expiry notifications.
settings.acmeRootCertificateHelp: If the ACME endpoint's TLS certificate is signed by an internal root not in the system trust store, paste the root (or chain) here so Caddy can connect to it.
settings.agentManagementUnavailableTitle: No agent is answering, so the container cannot be managed from here
settings.agentsDescription: An agent recreates, rebuilds and configures the Caddy container on its host. The controller has no Docker access of its own, and no address for any Caddy - everything reaches a proxy through its agent.
settings.autoPairingDisabledDescription: Unpairing the bundled agent turned auto-pairing off, so it stays idle instead of pairing itself straight back. Turn it on again to let it pair within a few seconds.
settings.passkeyHostnameWarningTitle: Passkeys are tied to this hostname
settings.passkeyHostnameWarningDescription: Every passkey registered here belongs to {host}. Change the Public URL to another hostname and none of them will sign in again: people use their password or single sign-on, then add a new passkey.
settings.autoPairingDisabledTitle: The bundled agent will not pair itself
settings.enableAutoPairing: Let the bundled agent pair itself
settings.repairBootstrapIssued: This is the bundled agent, so a token for it was left on the data volume. If it is idle it pairs itself within a few seconds. The token expires in 30 minutes.
settings.repairCodeHelp: Only this agent can use this code, and it replaces the agent's current secret. Valid for five minutes. Run this on that agent's host:
settings.analyticsCollectionHelp: Record every proxied request and every WAF event, and show them on the Analytics page. With this off, no events are written and the agents stop reading Caddy's logs.
settings.analyticsRetentionHelp: How long events are kept. Lowering it migrates the existing tables' TTL, which rewrites their parts.
settings.authentikDefaultsHelp: Host-level settings can override this default
settings.backChannelLogoutHelp: Optional. Set this as the provider's back-channel logout URL and CPM will end a user's sessions when the identity provider ends theirs.
settings.clickhouseUrlHelp: Where the analytics database is reachable.
settings.clientIpHeadersHelp: Headers Caddy reads the client IP from - one per line. Empty defaults to X-Forwarded-For. Set Cf-Connecting-Ip for Cloudflare, etc.
settings.dashboardCheckNeedsSaveDescription: The check asks the domain that is saved, not the one in the field. Save first, then check.
settings.dashboardCheckNeedsSaveTitle: Save the domain before checking it
settings.dashboardDisableConfirmBody: You are reading this page on {domain}, which is the domain about to stop being served. Saving will take this route away while you are using it.
settings.dashboardDisableConfirmRecovery: The dashboard stays reachable on the controller's own port - http://'<host>':3000 - which is where you would turn this back on.
settings.dashboardDisableConfirmTitle: This will end your current connection
settings.dashboardDnsMatchDescription: A request sent to that domain came back to this instance, signed. DNS, the network in between, and Caddy's route all work, so HTTPS has been switched on.
settings.dashboardDnsMismatchDescription: The domain resolves to {resolved}, but a request sent to it did not arrive here - it reached a different server, or nothing answered on port 80. HTTPS has been switched off; a certificate order would fail the same way.
settings.dashboardDnsMismatchTitle: The domain does not reach this instance
settings.dashboardDnsUnresolvedDescription: Nothing answers for that name yet. Create an A or AAAA record pointing at this deployment, then check again.
settings.dashboardDomainHelp: The name this dashboard answers on, once it is served through Caddy.
settings.dashboardEnabledHelp: Serves this dashboard through the Caddy this instance manages, as a host it maintains for you.
settings.dashboardProxyOptionsHelp: Everything a proxy host can be configured with, applied to this dashboard's route: certificate, access list, agents, headers, WAF, geo-blocking and the rest. The upstream is always this controller. CPM forward auth and mTLS access rules are not offered here, because they are stored against a proxy host.
settings.dashboardPortEscapeDescription: This host is generated from the settings above rather than stored in Proxy Hosts, so nothing can delete it by accident. The controller also publishes its own port, so http://'<host>':3000 reaches this page whatever happens to the route.
settings.dashboardPortEscapeTitle: You cannot lock yourself out with this
settings.dashboardTlsHelp: Forces HTTPS and asks Caddy for a certificate. Only useful once requests to the domain arrive here.
settings.dashboardTlsUnverifiedDescription: The last check did not confirm that this domain reaches here. Caddy will keep retrying the certificate order, and the domain will not serve over HTTPS until it succeeds.
settings.dashboardTlsUnverifiedTitle: HTTPS is on, but reachability was not confirmed
settings.defaultDomainHelp: Filled in for you when you create a proxy host, so the domain you use most is already there.
settings.defaultGeoblockTrustedProxies: Default geoblock trusted proxies from this list
settings.defaultRedirectStatusHelp: 307 and 308 preserve the original request method.
settings.defaultRedirectUrlHelp: Absolute, relative, and Caddy placeholder-based targets are supported.
settings.defaultResponseBehaviorHelp: Applied only when no configured proxy host matches the request.
settings.defaultResponseBodyHelp: Plain text, JSON, or custom HTML. Empty is allowed.
settings.defaultResponseHeadersHelp: Optional Name: value pairs, one per line. For custom HTML, set Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8.
settings.defaultResponsePriorityTitle: Configured hosts always run before this catch-all
settings.defaultResponseStatusHelp: Any final HTTP status from 200 through 599.
settings.defaultResponseTlsDescription: For HTTPS the response can only be sent once a TLS certificate completes the handshake, so an unknown hostname or direct IP may fail earlier.
settings.dnsAddressFamilyHelp: Both resolves AAAA + A with IPv6 preferred ordering.
settings.dnsPinningHelp: Resolves upstream hostnames at config-apply time and writes IPs into Caddy's active config.
settings.dnsPinningInfoDescription: Resolution happens at config save/reload time, and resolved IPs are written into Caddy's active config. If one handler has multiple different HTTPS upstream hostnames, HTTPS pinning is skipped for those HTTPS upstreams to avoid SNI mismatch.
settings.dnsProviderModuleDisabledDescription: Enable it under Settings → Caddy Build and rebuild Caddy before using it for DNS-01 challenges. Credentials saved now will not be used until then.
settings.dnsProviderModuleDisabledTitle: This provider's Caddy module is disabled
settings.dnsResolversInfoDescription: Useful when your DNS provider has slow propagation or when using split-horizon DNS. Common public resolvers: 1.1.1.1 (Cloudflare), 194.242.2.2 (Mullvad), 9.9.9.9 (Quad9).
settings.environmentOverrideTitle: Currently set by an environment variable
settings.ephemeralNodesHelp: Ephemeral nodes disappear from the tailnet when Caddy stops, instead of lingering as offline machines. Their identity is not reused, so a restart shows up as a new device.
settings.accentColorPinned: Set by {env}, which overrides what is stored here.
settings.faviconUploadHelp: PNG, ICO, SVG, WebP, GIF or JPEG, up to 256 KB. A square image of at least 32×32 works everywhere; browsers scale it down themselves.
settings.faviconTooltipReplace: Replace the favicon with another image
settings.faviconWillBeRemoved: The custom favicon will be removed when saved.
settings.geoblockTrustedProxiesHelp: Use these ranges as the default trusted-proxy list for global geoblocking so the two can't silently disagree. A geoblock list set explicitly wins.
settings.geoipBehind: MaxMind has a newer {editions} than the copy on disk, and it has not been downloaded yet.
settings.geoipDownloadsDescription: It checks MaxMind on the interval below using these credentials. Agents fetch the databases from this controller rather than each holding a licence key.
settings.geoipDownloadsTitle: This controller downloads the databases itself
settings.geoipHelp: Country lookups for analytics, and the country matching that geo blocking is built on. With this off, the geo block fields are marked as such and no country is recorded against an event.
settings.geoipNeverChecked: MaxMind has never been checked for updates.
settings.geoipSavedDisabled: GeoIP disabled. Country matching is no longer offered.
settings.geoipSavedEnabled: GeoIP enabled - downloading the databases from MaxMind.
settings.geoipSavedNeedsCredentials: GeoIP enabled. Add a MaxMind account ID and licence key to download the databases.
settings.geoipUpdateDisabled: Turn GeoIP on and save to download the databases.
settings.geoipUpdateIntervalHelp: MaxMind rebuilds GeoLite ASN daily, and Country and City on Tuesdays and Fridays. A check only downloads what changed.
settings.geoipUpdateUnconfigured: Add a MaxMind account ID and licence key to download the databases.
settings.globalErrorPagesHelp: These error pages apply to every proxy host as a fallback. A per-host error page for the same status code takes precedence.
settings.gravatarEnvironmentOverrideTitle: Gravatar is set by the AVATAR_GRAVATAR environment variable
settings.gravatarHelp: For users with no icon of their own, look one up from gravatar.com by their email address. Their browser contacts gravatar.com directly, which discloses their IP and a hash of their address to a third party. Accounts with a local-only address are never looked up, and anyone without a Gravatar falls back to their initial.
settings.gravatarLabel: Use Gravatar when a user has no icon
settings.groupMappingHelp: Derive CPM roles and groups from the identity provider's group claim.
settings.groupPrefixHelp: Shorthand for naming the role groups: with prefix CPM_, members of CPM_Admin become admins, CPM_User users and CPM_Viewer viewers. Name the groups below instead if they do not share a prefix.
settings.groupSyncHelp: Creates CPM groups from the remaining prefixed claims (with the prefix stripped) for forward-auth access control. Groups you created yourself are never modified.
settings.groupsClaimHelp: Claim holding the user's groups. Use dots for nested claims, e.g. resource_access.cpm.roles. Remember to request a matching scope above.
settings.homeAttentionCount: {count, plural, one {# setting is} other {# settings are}} configured but not working as intended
settings.imageRepositoryHelp: Where this deployment's images come from, without the image name. Point it at your own namespace if you run a fork, or it will report releases you cannot pull.
settings.issuerUrlHelp: For OIDC providers, the issuer URL enables automatic discovery of endpoints.
settings.legacyPasswordResetHelp: New passwords are hashed with argon2id. Accounts created before that change still use bcrypt, which caps the password at 72 bytes. Turning this on sends those users to a reset screen at their next sign-in; choosing a new password upgrades the hash and clears the prompt. Users who sign in through an OAuth/OIDC provider have no password and are never asked.
settings.legacyPasswordResetLabel: Require a password change for users still on an older hash
settings.localAgentDescription: It is reached over a socket on the shared data volume and needs no pairing. Pair a remote agent below only if Caddy runs on a different host from this controller.
settings.managedAnalyticsTitle: The agent starts and stops ClickHouse for you
settings.maxmindCredentialsHelp: From your MaxMind account. Without a subscription the databases cannot be downloaded, though GeoIP still works if you supply the files another way.
settings.metricsEndpointHelp: Prometheus-compatible scrape endpoint, exposed on a dedicated port.
settings.metricsInfoTitle: Point your monitoring tool at the metrics endpoint
settings.metricsPortHelp: Separate from the admin API on port 2019.
settings.name: Name
settings.oauthAutoLinkHelp: Signing in through this provider attaches to the existing user with the same email address. When off, users link it themselves from their profile.
settings.forwardAuthSequentialIdsTitle: Forward auth still sends numeric user IDs
settings.forwardAuthSequentialIdsDescription: Applications behind forward auth receive each account's sequential number as X-CPM-User-Id, which reveals how many accounts exist. Once none of them keys its accounts on that number, turn off {setting} below to send a UUID instead.
settings.forwardAuthSequentialIdsDismiss: Dismiss the numeric user ID notice
settings.pairingCodeExpires: {minutes, plural, one {Valid for # more minute.} other {Valid for # more minutes.}}
settings.pairingCodeFailed: Could not generate a pairing code.
settings.pairingCodeHelp: Generate a code here, then run the pair command on the agent's host. The code is valid for five minutes and works once.
settings.pairingCodeRun: Run this on the agent's host, then confirm the controller name it shows:
settings.passwordPolicyEnvironmentOverrideTitle: This policy is set by the AUTH_REQUIRE_PASSWORD_CHANGE_ON_LEGACY_HASH environment variable
settings.providersEmptyDescription: Add a provider to enable single sign-on.

account_lock_base_delay_ms.description: How long the first lock lasts. Each failure after it doubles the wait.
account_lock_base_delay_ms.label: First account lock (milliseconds)

account_lock_disable_after.description: Counted like the lock above: forgotten a day after the last failure, and reset by a successful sign-in.
account_lock_disable_after.label: Failed sign-ins before an account is disabled

account_lock_disable_enabled.description: Disable an account once it reaches the number of failed sign-ins below, until an administrator enables it again. Anyone who knows a username can then disable that account by guessing at it. The last active administrator is never disabled, only locked.
account_lock_disable_enabled.label: Disable accounts after repeated failed sign-ins

account_lock_enabled.description: Slow down guesses at one account whatever address they come from. Separate from the per-client lockout above.
account_lock_enabled.label: Lock accounts after failed sign-ins

account_lock_free_failures.description: How many failures an account takes before each further one locks it.
account_lock_free_failures.label: Failed sign-ins before an account is locked

account_lock_max_delay_ms.description: The doubling stops here, so guessing can slow the owner's sign-in but never shut it off.
account_lock_max_delay_ms.label: Longest account lock (milliseconds)

analytics_enabled.description: Collect traffic and WAF events. With an agent running the stack, turning this on also starts the ClickHouse container - no Compose profile needed. If left unset, analytics is on only when a password is configured below.
analytics_enabled.label: Enable analytics

accent_color.description: The colour of selected items, primary buttons and focus rings across the dashboard.
accent_color.label: Accent colour

app_name.description: Shown in the sidebar, on the login card, and as the suffix on every page title.
app_name.label: Application name

auth_allow_oauth_registration.description: Let a first-time OAuth identity create an account. Separate from self-registration: with this off, existing users can still sign in and link.
auth_allow_oauth_registration.label: Allow OAuth registration

auth_allow_oauth_role_from_claims.description: Let the provider's claims set a new user's role and status. With this off they are forced to user/active regardless of what the IdP sends. Only enable it for an IdP you control.
auth_allow_oauth_role_from_claims.label: Trust IdP role claims

auth_allow_self_registration.description: Let anyone create an account with an email address and password.
auth_allow_self_registration.label: Allow self-registration

auth_disable_local_users.description: Remove local accounts entirely: no credential sign-in, no password management, no bootstrap admin. Enable only once OAuth sign-in is confirmed working.
auth_disable_local_users.label: OIDC-only mode

auth_rate_limit_enabled.description: Throttle requests to the auth endpoints. Separate from the login throttle below.
auth_rate_limit_enabled.label: Rate-limit auth requests

auth_rate_limit_max.description: How many auth requests one client may make before being throttled.
auth_rate_limit_max.label: Auth requests per window

auth_rate_limit_window.description: The period over which auth requests are counted.
auth_rate_limit_window.label: Auth rate-limit window (seconds)

auth_require_password_change_on_legacy_h.description: Require anyone still on a pre-argon2id bcrypt hash to change their password. Leave unset to let the Security toggle decide.
auth_require_password_change_on_legacy_h.label: Force a reset for legacy password hashes

auth_trust_host.description: Build URLs from the request's Host header. Only behind a proxy that rewrites it, and only when the public URL above cannot cover the setup.
auth_trust_host.label: Trust the Host header

avatar_gravatar.description: Let user icons fall back to gravatar.com, which the browser fetches directly. Turn off to keep every avatar lookup off the network.
avatar_gravatar.label: Gravatar fallback

base_url.description: The address users reach this instance at. OAuth redirect URIs are built from it, so it must match what the provider has registered.
base_url.label: Public URL

caddy_api_url.description: Where Caddy's admin API is reachable, for a deployment running Caddy with no agent. With an agent, every admin call is proxied through it and this is not used.
caddy_api_url.label: Caddy admin API

caddy_monitor_enabled.label: Re-apply after a Caddy restart
caddy_monitor_enabled.description: Watch every Caddy for a restart onto a config this controller did not send, and push its configuration back. Turn it off only on a controller sharing a Caddy it does not own, or the two push their own idea of the config at each other every pass.

caddy_build_timeout.description: How long to wait for an xcaddy rebuild before giving up. Caddy compiles from source, so slow or ARM hosts can take considerably longer than the default.
caddy_build_timeout.label: Caddy build timeout (seconds)

clickhouse_db.description: The database traffic and WAF events are written to.
clickhouse_db.label: ClickHouse database

clickhouse_password.description: Required for analytics: the ClickHouse container refuses to start without one, and with it empty there is nothing to authenticate as.
clickhouse_password.label: ClickHouse password

clickhouse_retention_days.description: How long traffic and WAF events are kept. Lowering it uses less disk, and migrates the existing tables' TTL on the next start.
clickhouse_retention_days.label: Analytics retention (days)

clickhouse_url.description: Where the analytics database is reachable.
clickhouse_url.label: ClickHouse URL

clickhouse_user.description: The account traffic and WAF events are written as.
clickhouse_user.label: ClickHouse user

forward_auth_allowed_ports.description: Non-default ports that CPM forward-auth sites are served on, comma-separated. Caddy matches a host whatever the port, so a sign-in on a port that is neither listed here nor the default for http or https is refused.
forward_auth_allowed_ports.label: Forward-auth ports

forward_auth_sequential_user_ids.description: Send X-CPM-User-Id as the sequential account number instead of a UUID. Sequential ids reveal how many accounts exist. Changing this changes the id every upstream sees for every user.
forward_auth_sequential_user_ids.label: Numeric forward-auth user IDs

forward_auth_internal_url.description: The address Caddy uses to reach this app for forward_auth. Derived from the container network when empty; set it only if that derivation is wrong.
forward_auth_internal_url.label: Internal forward-auth address

geoip_enabled.description: Country lookups for analytics and geo blocking. If a MaxMind account ID and licence key are set, turning this on also makes the controller download the databases. If left unset, GeoIP is on only when the databases are already present.
geoip_enabled.label: Enable GeoIP

geoip_update_interval_hours.description: How often the controller asks MaxMind for newer databases. MaxMind rebuilds GeoLite ASN daily, and Country and City on Tuesdays and Fridays. A check downloads only what changed.
geoip_update_interval_hours.label: Update check interval (hours)

geoipupdate_account_id.description: Needed to download GeoLite2 databases, which geo blocking depends on.
geoipupdate_account_id.label: MaxMind account ID

geoipupdate_license_key.description: Issued alongside the account ID at maxmind.com.
geoipupdate_license_key.label: MaxMind licence key

login_block_ms.description: How long a blocked client stays blocked.
login_block_ms.label: Lockout duration (milliseconds)

login_max_attempts.description: How many failed sign-ins one client may make before it is blocked.
login_max_attempts.label: Failed logins before lockout

login_window_ms.description: The period over which failed sign-ins are counted.
login_window_ms.label: Login window (milliseconds)

update_check_enabled.description: Ask the registry below, a few times a day, whether a newer release has been published. Turn it off to make no such request; the CRS plugin registry check and GeoIP downloads have switches of their own.
update_check_enabled.label: Check for updates

update_image_repository.description: Where this deployment's images come from, without the image name - the update check reads its tags. Point it at your own namespace if you run a fork, or it will report releases you cannot pull.
update_image_repository.label: Image repository

smtp_enabled.description: Password reset links, invitations and certificate alerts go out through the SMTP server below. If left unset, email is on whenever a server is named.
smtp_enabled.label: Send email

smtp_host.description: The host name or address of the mail server to relay through.
smtp_host.label: SMTP server

smtp_port.description: Usually 587 for STARTTLS, 465 for implicit TLS and 25 for an unencrypted relay.
smtp_port.label: SMTP port

smtp_security.description: starttls upgrades the connection and refuses a server that cannot; tls encrypts from the first byte; none sends in the clear, for a relay on a trusted network only.
smtp_security.label: SMTP encryption

smtp_username.description: Leave empty for a relay that accepts mail without signing in.
smtp_username.label: SMTP username

smtp_password.description: Sent only after the connection is encrypted, unless encryption is set to none.
smtp_password.label: SMTP password

smtp_from.description: The From address on every message, shown under the application name. Many servers refuse one the account is not allowed to send as.
smtp_from.label: Sender address

email_alert_recipients.description: Comma-separated addresses for certificate alerts, and extra recipients of every notification. If left empty, certificate alerts go to every active administrator.
email_alert_recipients.label: Alert recipients

certificate_expiry_alert_days.description: Email the alert recipients once a certificate has fewer days than this left. Caddy renews on its own well before then, so an alert means renewal is failing. 0 turns alerts off.
certificate_expiry_alert_days.label: Certificate alert threshold (days)

notify_account_disabled.description: When an account is disabled after failed sign-ins, or the last administrator is kept enabled.
notify_account_disabled.label: Account disabled after failed sign-ins

notify_admin_locked.description: When failed sign-ins lock an administrator's account.
notify_admin_locked.label: Administrator account locked

notify_admin_added.description: When an administrator account is created, or a user is made an administrator.
notify_admin_added.label: New administrator

notify_agent_offline.description: When an agent stays disconnected longer than the time below, and when it is back.
notify_agent_offline.label: Agent offline

notify_agent_offline_minutes.description: How long an agent may be disconnected before anyone is told. After a restart of this server every agent gets this long to reconnect.
notify_agent_offline_minutes.label: Agent offline after (minutes)

notify_upstream_errors.description: When a proxy host answers 502, 503 or 504 as often as set below, and when it has been quiet for as long again. Read from the access log, so access logging must be on.
notify_upstream_errors.label: Upstream errors

notify_upstream_error_count.description: How many 502, 503 or 504 responses from one host, within the minutes below.
notify_upstream_error_count.label: Upstream errors before telling (responses)

notify_upstream_error_minutes.description: Also how long a host must go without one before it counts as recovered.
notify_upstream_error_minutes.label: Upstream error window (minutes)

notify_caddy_apply.description: When Caddy refuses a configuration, and when it loads one again. An unreachable Caddy is the agent's to report.
notify_caddy_apply.label: Caddy configuration refused

notify_agent_problems.description: When an agent reports a failed Caddy build, optional service or L4 port change, or log files it cannot read or prune.
notify_agent_problems.label: Agent failures

notify_geoip_failed.description: When the GeoIP database update has failed three times in a row, and when it works again.
notify_geoip_failed.label: GeoIP update failing

notify_crs_plugin_disabled.description: When a CRS plugin Caddy refuses is switched off so the rest of the configuration loads.
notify_crs_plugin_disabled.label: CRS plugin switched off

notify_update_available.description: Once per release, while the update check under General is on.
notify_update_available.label: New release

notify_disabled_account_owner.description: Email one message to an account's own address when it is disabled, by an administrator or after failed sign-ins. A disabled account gets nothing else.
notify_disabled_account_owner.label: Tell the owner of a disabled account

settings.reviewDiffStat: +{added, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}}, -{removed, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}}
settings.reviewNoConfigChange: These settings do not change the Caddy config.
settings.reviewSecretsMasked: Credentials are masked in this view.
settings.reviewSubtitle: Revision #{from} to #{to} - nothing has reached Caddy yet.
settings.reviewUnchangedLines: {count, plural, one {# unchanged line} other {# unchanged lines}}

history.title: Revision history
history.subtitle: Every apply to Caddy, newest first. Compare any two revisions, or restore an earlier one.
history.notRecordedHelp: Applied before revisions kept their values, so it can be neither compared nor restored.
history.same: Pick two different revisions to compare.
history.noChanges: These revisions hold the same settings.
history.configNote: Rendered against today's hosts, so only the settings differ between the two sides.
history.configFailed: The Caddy config could not be rendered for these revisions.
history.notComparable: A revision in this range was applied before values were recorded, so it cannot be compared.
history.restoreHelp: Stages the settings revision #{id} had, on top of anything you already have pending. Review and apply them like any other change.
history.restoreStaged: {count, plural, =0 {Revision #{id} matches the current settings - nothing to restore.} one {# change staged. Review and apply to restore revision #{id}.} other {# changes staged. Review and apply to restore revision #{id}.}}

settings.roleGroupNamesHelp: Name the groups exactly as your provider reports them. Separate several with commas - platform-owners, sre-oncall - and any one of them grants the role. A role left blank falls back to the prefix above, so the two styles can be mixed. The most privileged match wins.
settings.roleMappingAuthorityHelp: The provider becomes authoritative: a user who loses the admin group is demoted on their next sign-in. The last remaining admin is never demoted.
settings.sharedAgentConfigTitle: Every agent runs the same configuration
settings.stagedSaved: Staged. Review and apply to send it to Caddy.
settings.storedCredentialsHelp: Leave fields blank to keep existing values.
settings.storedSecretHelp: A secret is configured. Its existing value cannot be viewed.
settings.strictTrustedProxiesHelp: Only trust the client IP headers from the configured proxies, rejecting spoofed values from untrusted peers.
settings.tailscaleControlServerHelp: Point at a Headscale or other coordination server. Empty uses Tailscale's own.
settings.tailscaleDefaultNodeHelp: The tailnet machine name used by hosts that do not name one of their own. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
settings.tailscaleHttp3Help: Lets clients on the tailnet reach served hosts over QUIC. Off by default; the global HTTP/3 setting must also be on.
settings.tailscaleHttp3WarningBody: With HTTP/3 on, Caddy has to reach the control server while it loads a configuration. Whenever the control server is unreachable, that load can hang and lock Caddy's admin API, so no proxy host on this agent can be updated until it comes back.
settings.tailscaleHttp3WarningTitle: HTTP/3 can hang Caddy's config load
settings.tailscaleHelp: Runs a Tailscale node inside Caddy. A proxy host can then be served privately on your tailnet, gated on tailnet identity, or proxied to a backend that only exists on the tailnet.
settings.tailscaleKeyValidationDisabledTitle: Auth keys are not being checked
settings.tailscaleKeyValidationHelp: Catches a revoked, expired or mistyped key here instead of at the next config apply. Needs a Tailscale API access token, because an auth key cannot authenticate to the API.
settings.tailscaleKeyValidationLabel: Check the auth key against the Tailscale API before saving
settings.tailscaleModuleDisabledTitle: The Tailscale module is not enabled
settings.tailscaleStateDirectoryHelp: Where each node keeps its identity, one subdirectory per node. Must be on a volume, or every restart registers a new machine.
settings.trustedProxiesInfoDescription: This fixes client-IP attribution everywhere at once - access logs, analytics, the country map, and any downstream handler using the client_ip placeholder.
settings.trustedProxiesInfoTitle: Nothing else on the host has to change
settings.trustedProxiesScopeDescription: Applied to the main HTTP server
settings.requireAdminTwoFactorHelp: An administrator who signs in with a password and hasn't set up an authenticator app is sent to do that before anything else. Single sign-on accounts are left to their identity provider.
settings.http2Help: Offer HTTP/2 over TLS. HTTP/1.1 is always available, so clients that can't use it still connect

dnsDelegation.title: Challenge delegation
dnsDelegation.description: Point _acme-challenge at a zone a DNS provider can write, and DNS-01 works for domains whose own DNS has no API. Each name under a delegated domain needs the same CNAME; a wildcard uses its parent's. For a self-hosted BIND server, use the RFC2136 provider instead.

dnsDelegation.noCnameNeeded: None - this row only picks the provider
dnsDelegation.cnameMissingTitle: Some CNAMEs are missing or point elsewhere
dnsDelegation.cnameMissingDescription: Challenges for those names fail until the record exists. This checks from this server's resolver, which may not see what the certificate authority sees.
dnsDelegation.domainHelp: Covers this name and every name under it. The longest matching domain wins.
dnsDelegation.targetHelp: The name _acme-challenge points to; the challenge record is written there. Leave empty to only choose a provider.
dnsDelegation.providerHelp: Writes the challenge record. Default uses a certificate's own provider, then the default one.
dnsDelegation.rfc2136Hint: There is no manual DNS mode: a record typed by hand would need retyping at every renewal. Delegate to a zone with an API, or to acme-dns below.
dnsDelegation.registerDescription: Creates an account on an acme-dns server for one domain and delegates that domain to it. The account's password is stored encrypted.
dnsDelegation.registerDomainHelp: The domain the account answers for; a wildcard shares its account.
dnsDelegation.serverUrlHelp: HTTPS, unless the server is on a private address or a single-label name such as a Compose service. Your own server is better than a public one.
dnsDelegation.registeredTitle: Registered. Create this record at your DNS host:
dnsDelegation.registeredDescription: Certificates for this domain use the account once the change is applied and the record exists.

captcha.secretKeyHelp: Used by this server to check each solve with the provider. Stored encrypted.
captcha.secretKeyStored: A secret key is stored. Leave blank to keep it.
captcha.capInstanceUrlHelp: Where your Cap Standalone server is reached by browsers and by this server, without the site key.
captcha.oidcOnlyBody: There is no username step while local accounts are disabled, so the CAPTCHA only applies once they are enabled again.

crowdsec.enabledHelp: Every proxy host and L4 host refuses addresses the Local API has a decision against, unless the host opts out in its editor. A ban or captcha decision answers 403, a throttle decision 429 with Retry-After. Decisions are kept in Caddy's memory, so a lookup never waits on the Local API.
crowdsec.moduleDisabledTitle: The CrowdSec module is not in Caddy
crowdsec.moduleDisabledBody: These settings are kept, but nothing is checked until it is: {reason}
crowdsec.apiUrlHelp: Where Caddy reaches your CrowdSec Local API, such as http://crowdsec:8080. Plain http only for a private address, since the bouncer key travels with every request.
crowdsec.apiKeyCreate: Create one on the CrowdSec host:
crowdsec.apiKeyHelp: Stored encrypted and never shown again. A Caddy placeholder such as '{env.CROWDSEC_API_KEY}' works too, and keeps the key out of the database.
crowdsec.apiKeyStored: A bouncer key is stored. Leave blank to keep it.
crowdsec.apiKeyReenter: A bouncer key is stored, but it is only kept while both addresses stay the same. Enter it again.
crowdsec.tickerIntervalHelp: How often Caddy pulls new decisions from the Local API, from 1s to 24h. A new ban takes up to this long to apply.
crowdsec.appsecUrlHelp: Optional. Where Caddy reaches the CrowdSec AppSec component, such as http://crowdsec:7422. Every request is then also sent there for inspection, after rate limiting and geo blocking.
crowdsec.appsecFailOpen: Let requests through when AppSec is unavailable
crowdsec.appsecFailOpenHelp: Off by default: while AppSec cannot be reached or answers with an error, requests are refused.
crowdsec.trustedProxiesTitle: Decisions match the real client address
crowdsec.trustedProxiesBody: The bouncer reads the client IP after Settings > Network > Trusted Proxies has been applied. Behind a load balancer or CDN, trust its ranges there, or every request is matched on the proxy's address.
crowdsec.modeHelp: Managed runs CrowdSec in a container beside Caddy, started by the bundled agent and fed Caddy's access log, which stays on and in JSON while it is managed. External uses a CrowdSec you run yourself.
crowdsec.onlineApi: Share signals with CrowdSec's Central API
crowdsec.onlineApiHelp: Off by default. On, the container registers with CrowdSec, sends it the addresses it decides against and receives the community blocklist in return. Off, nothing leaves this host but the downloads of CrowdSec's detection rules.
crowdsec.managedAppsecHelp: Every request on an HTTP host is also sent to the container's AppSec component, with CrowdSec's virtual patching and generic rules, after rate limiting and geo blocking.
crowdsec.managedRemoteTitle: Only hosts served by the bundled agent are checked
crowdsec.managedRemoteBody: Caddy on another agent's host cannot reach this container, so its hosts are served unchecked in this mode. To cover them, run CrowdSec yourself and choose External.
crowdsec.managedPendingBody: The bundled agent starts the container when these settings are applied. Its first start downloads the image and CrowdSec's detection rules, which takes a few minutes; Caddy serves unchecked until then.
crowdsec.managedNoAgentTitle: No agent is running the container
crowdsec.managedNoAgentBody: The bundled agent is not connected. It starts the container when it reconnects.

ldap.emptyDescription: Add an LDAP or Active Directory server, and its users sign in on the normal sign-in form with their directory password.
ldap.deleteConfirm: Delete {name}? Its users keep their accounts, but can no longer sign in with their directory password. Those with no other way in also lose their passkeys and are signed out.
ldap.name: Name
ldap.nameHelp: Shown on the sign-in form when there is more than one directory.
ldap.urlHelp: ldaps://host:636, or ldap://host:389 with StartTLS. Only this address is ever dialled.
ldap.startTlsHelp: Upgrade an ldap:// connection to TLS. If the server refuses, the sign-in fails; it never continues unencrypted.
ldap.tlsVerifyHelp: Against the system's certificate authorities and the one below.
ldap.tlsUnverifiedTitle: The server's identity is not checked
ldap.tlsUnverifiedDescription: Anyone who can intercept the connection can read every password typed on the sign-in form. Add the directory's CA certificate below instead.
ldap.caPemHelp: PEM, for a directory whose certificate comes from a private CA. Trusted in addition to the system's.
ldap.modeServiceAccount: A service account finds the user
ldap.modeServiceAccountHelp: A read-only account, or an anonymous search, finds the user's entry and reads their groups; the user's password is then checked with a bind of its own.
ldap.modeUserBindHelp: No service account. The typed username becomes a bind name, and everything else is read with the user's own rights. The recommended Active Directory setup when there is no service account; it needs ldaps:// or StartTLS.
ldap.dnTemplateHelp: Where the typed username replaces '{username}'. A DN such as uid='{username}',ou=people,dc=example,dc=org, escaped; or for Active Directory a UPN such as '{username}'@ad.example.org or a down-level name such as EXAMPLE\'{username}', where a username may hold only letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores.
ldap.userBindFilterHelp: Finds the user's own entry after the bind, which must be the account that signed in. The typed username replaces '{username}', escaped.
ldap.bindDnHelp: A read-only service account that searches for users. Leave empty for an anonymous search.
ldap.bindPasswordStoredHelp: Stored. Leave empty to keep it; changing the address or bind DN needs it typed again.
ldap.userFilterHelp: Must match exactly one entry. The typed username replaces '{username}', escaped.
ldap.groupSourceSearch: Search for groups naming the user
ldap.groupFilterHelp: The user's DN replaces '{dn}'. Active Directory's nested form is (member:1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941:='{dn}').
ldap.autoLinkHelp: A first sign-in joins an existing account with the same email address. Only turn this on when the directory's email addresses are set by administrators, not by users: whoever holds an address takes over that account, administrators included.
ldap.groupMappingHelp: Group names are the first part of each group's DN, such as Proxy Admins for CN=Proxy Admins,OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=org. Nested groups count with Active Directory's group filter.

test.connected: Connected, and the service account can read the base DN.

test.signedIn: Connected, and the test user signed in.

setup.dashboardEnabledHelp: Serves this dashboard through the Caddy this instance manages, over HTTP to begin with. Port 3000 keeps working either way.
setup.defaultDomainHelp: Offered first when you create a proxy host, so the one you use most belongs here.
setup.emptyDatabaseRequiredDescription: This copies rows with their original identifiers, so it expects nothing to have been created here yet. Running it against a database that is already in use is not supported.

accountDisabled.intro: The account {email} on {appName} has been disabled. You cannot sign in with it until an administrator enables it again.
accountDisabled.byFailedSignIns: It was disabled after {failures} failed sign-ins in a row. If those were not you, someone may be guessing your password; tell an administrator.
accountDisabled.nothingElse: This is the only message this account will receive while it is disabled.

invite.subject: You have been invited to {appName}
invite.signIn: Your username is {username}. Choose a password to sign in with.
invite.expiry: The link works once, within {days} days. Ask for a new invitation if it runs out.

certificateAlert.subject: {count, plural, one {A certificate needs} other {# certificates need}} attention on {appName}
certificateAlert.intro: These certificates expire within {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, or already have:
certificateAlert.expiring: {name} ({where}) expires on {date}, in {days, plural, =0 {less than a day} one {# day} other {# days}}
certificateAlert.once: Each certificate is reported once as it nears expiry and once more if it expires.

notifications.intro: {count, plural, one {Something happened} other {# things happened}} on {appName} that an administrator should know about:
notifications.manage: Sent to the notification recipients, or every active administrator when none are set. Choose what is sent under Settings → Email → Notifications.

accountDisabled.title: Account disabled after failed sign-ins
accountDisabled.item: {email} was disabled after {failures} failed sign-ins. An administrator must enable it again, from Users or with cpm-server --enable-user.

lastAdminKept.title: Last administrator kept enabled
lastAdminKept.item: {email} reached {failures} failed sign-ins but is the last active administrator, so it was not disabled. It stays on the timed lock.

adminLocked.title: Administrator account locked
adminLocked.item: The administrator account {email} was locked after {failures} failed sign-ins. Each further failure locks it for longer.

adminAdded.title: {promoted, select, yes {User made an administrator} other {New administrator account}}
adminAdded.item: {promoted, select, yes {{email} was made an administrator.} other {A new administrator account was created: {email}.}}

agentOffline.title: Agent {agent} is offline
agentOffline.item: The agent {agent} has been disconnected for more than {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}. Its Caddy keeps its last configuration but gets no changes.

upstreamErrors.title: Upstream errors on {host}
upstreamErrors.item: {host} answered {count, plural, one {# request} other {# requests}} with 502, 503 or 504 within {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}. Its upstream may be down.

upstreamRecovered.title: {host} has recovered
upstreamRecovered.item: {host} has answered no 502, 503 or 504 for a while.

caddyApplyFailed.title: {scope, select, agent {Caddy on {agent} refused its configuration} other {Caddy refused its configuration}}
caddyApplyFailed.item: {scope, select, agent {Caddy on {agent} did not load its configuration: {error}} other {Caddy did not load its configuration: {error}}}. It keeps serving the last one it loaded.

caddyApplyRecovered.title: {scope, select, agent {Caddy on {agent} loads its configuration again} other {Caddy loads its configuration again}}
caddyApplyRecovered.item: {scope, select, agent {Caddy on {agent} loaded its configuration again.} other {Caddy loaded its configuration again.}}

agentProblem.title: {problem, select, caddyBuild {Caddy build failed} services {Optional service failed} l4Ports {L4 port change failed} other {Log files need attention}} on {agent}
agentProblem.item: {problem, select, caddyBuild {The Caddy image build failed on {agent}} services {Starting or stopping ClickHouse or CrowdSec failed on {agent}} l4Ports {Changing the L4 ports failed on {agent}} other {Caddy's log files on {agent} cannot be read or pruned, so its disk may fill}}

agentProblemResolved.title: {problem, select, caddyBuild {Caddy build works again} services {Optional services work again} l4Ports {L4 ports work again} other {Log files are fine again}} on {agent}
agentProblemResolved.item: {problem, select, caddyBuild {The Caddy image on {agent} was built.} services {The optional services on {agent} were applied.} l4Ports {The L4 ports on {agent} were applied.} other {Caddy's log files on {agent} can be read and pruned again.}}

geoipFailed.title: GeoIP update keeps failing
geoipFailed.item: The GeoIP database update failed {failures} times in a row: {error}. Geo-blocking keeps using the databases already downloaded.

geoipRecovered.title: GeoIP update works again
geoipRecovered.item: The GeoIP database update succeeded again.

crsPluginDisabled.title: CRS plugin {plugin} switched off
crsPluginDisabled.item: Caddy refused the WAF with the CRS plugin {plugin} {version}, so it was switched off and the rest of the configuration loaded. It stays off until it is turned on again from the WAF page.

updateAvailable.title: Version {version} is available
updateAvailable.item: Release {version} is available. This instance runs {current}.

test.title: test notification
test.item: This is a test notification: administrator notifications reach this address.
